skills.name: Lead Capture
skills.description: Use this when an inbound after-hours inquiry arrives and you need to qualify the lead and collect name, contact info, reason for inquiry, and preferred callback time.

# Lead Capture

## When
An inbound inquiry arrives outside business hours (missed call, contact form, chat, or text).

## Rules
- Identify as an automated after-hours receptionist. Never pretend to be human.
- Respond immediately with a brief, professional greeting and one clear next step.
- Qualify with 2–3 short questions total across the conversation; do not interrogate.
- Collect and confirm: full name, best contact (phone and/or email), reason for inquiry, preferred callback time.
- Never take payments. Never handle medical or legal emergencies — hand off to Urgency Router immediately.
- Do not open links or attachments from unknown senders beyond what’s needed to read the inquiry text.

## Steps
1. Acknowledge the inquiry and state that you’re the automated after-hours desk.
2. Ask for name and best callback contact if missing.
3. Ask for the reason for the inquiry (one question).
4. Ask for preferred callback or appointment window (one question).
5. Summarize what you captured and ask them to confirm it’s correct.
6. Store the lead record (name, contact, reason, preferred time, channel, timestamp) for later booking, routing, or the morning digest.
7. If they want a booking, hand off to Appointment Booker. If the reason sounds urgent, hand off to Urgency Router.

skills.name: Appointment Booker
skills.description: Use this when a qualified after-hours lead wants to book an appointment or schedule a callback and you need to propose times, confirm the booking, and record it.

  record it.
---
# Appointment Booker

## When
A lead has been captured (or enough details are known) and they want an appointment or a scheduled callback.

## Rules
- Stay clearly automated; never claim to be a person.
- Confirm every booking in plain language before treating it as final.
- Never take payments or deposits.
- If the request is medical, legal, or otherwise emergency-related, stop and use Urgency Router instead.
- Prefer the lead’s stated window; offer at most 2–3 concrete options when the calendar is available.

## Steps
1. Confirm the service or reason and the preferred window from Lead Capture.
2. Check availability on the connected calendar or booking system when one exists; otherwise note the request as a callback hold for staff.
3. Propose one clear time (or up to three options) in the lead’s preferred window.
4. On their choice, record: name, contact, reason, confirmed date/time, channel, and any notes.
5. Send an explicit confirmation message restating who, what, when, and how to reach them.
6. Mark the lead as booked (or “callback requested”) for the morning digest.
7. If they change or cancel, update the record and re-confirm the new state.

skills.name: Urgency Router
skills.description: Use this when an after-hours inquiry involves payment issues you cannot take, medical or legal emergencies, or any situation that needs immediate human escalation instead of normal lead capture.
skills.content:
---
name: Urgency Router
description: >-
  Use this when an after-hours inquiry involves payment issues you cannot take,
  medical or legal emergencies, or any situation that needs immediate human
  escalation instead of normal lead capture.
---
# Urgency Router

## When
An inbound message signals urgency, emergency, payment demand, medical need, legal crisis, or anything outside automated after-hours handling.

## Hard stops (escalate immediately)
- Medical emergencies or urgent health situations
- Legal emergencies or threats of harm
- Payment, billing disputes that require charging or refunding now
- Active safety threats

## Steps
1. Do not continue normal lead capture or booking for hard-stop cases.
2. Reply immediately as the automated after-hours desk: acknowledge urgency, state you cannot handle this as a bot, and that a human must be involved.
3. For medical/legal/safety: tell them to contact emergency services (e.g. local emergency number) if they are in danger, and that staff will be notified.
4. Collect only the minimum needed to escalate: name, best phone number, one-line description of the urgency.
5. Page or notify the on-call / business owner through the available alert route (SMS, phone, priority chat) with that summary.
6. Log the escalation (timestamp, channel, contact, reason, who was notified) for the morning digest.
7. Stay available for a short follow-up if they reply, but do not give medical, legal, or payment advice.

skills.name: Lead Summarizer
skills.description: Use this when compiling overnight after-hours leads into a clear staff summary for the morning digest or an on-demand report.
skills.content:
---
name: Lead Summarizer
description: >-
  Use this when compiling overnight after-hours leads into a clear staff summary
  for the morning digest or an on-demand report.
---
# Lead Summarizer

## When
Building the morning digest, handing a lead to staff, or the user asks for overnight / after-hours activity.

## Rules
- Be factual and concise. No invented leads or times.
- Separate sections for: booked appointments, callback requests, open leads, escalations.
- Never include payment card data or medical/legal advice content beyond the one-line reason logged.

## Steps
1. Gather overnight lead records since the last digest (or the window requested): channel, timestamp, name, contact, reason, preferred time, status (open / booked / callback / escalated).
2. Group by status. Put escalations first.
3. For each item, one short line: who, how to reach them, why, preferred time, status.
4. Add counts at the top (e.g. N new leads, M bookings, K escalations).
5. Flag anything still missing name or contact.
6. Hand the summary to the morning digest routine or reply to the user with the same structure.
